Mid-Gloucestershire Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Miss G. Johnson, 21, Eastgate Street, Gloucester.

January 9th.—A most enjoyable and successful Thé Dansant was held at the Mercers Hall, Gloucester. Dancing commenced at 3 p.m., and continued until 8 p.m., with an interval for a dainty tea, which everyone enjoyed.
February 12th.—Mr. F. H. Corson, City Electrical En- gineer, Gloucester, gave us another interesting and instructive demonstration lecture on "The Treatment of Minor Troubles which may arise in Domestic Apparatus," showing what happens when an electric kettle boils dry, and how modern kettles disconnect themselves. Mr. Corson also showed the working of an electric iron and radiator, and dealt with the replacement of fuses, wiring of lampholders, etc. Delightful souvenir of leatherette cases containing 5 and 10 amp. fuse wires were given to the members.
February 25th.—Our First Annual Meeting and Luncheon was held at the Mercers Hall, Gloucester, when we were delighted to have the Director with us. The Annual General Meeting was presided over by the Chairman (Mrs. Ellis), in the unavoidable absence of our President (the Countess of Berkeley), who was in Rome. The Director briefly outlined the work of the Association.
The Luncheon proved a very delightful and pleasing function. We were fortunate in having among our guests the Mayor and Mayoress of Gloucester, Mr. W. T. Hobbs, Mr. F. H. Corson, Mr. and Mrs. W. J. Bache (Cheltenham), Mr. H. S. Ellis, Mr. P. Gale and Mrs. R. J. Morris, the Deputy Lady Chairman and Hon. Secretary of the Cardiff Branch, the Vice-President and Hon. Secretary of the Chel- tenham Branch, and the Chairmen of the Bristol Branch. Toasts were very heartily proposed and responded to. Following the Luncheon a most interesting Lantern Lecture was given by Mr. H. S. Ellis on "The Development of an Electrical Power Company."
G. JOHNSON.

***

North Staffordshire Branch.
Joint Hon. Secretaries:
Mrs. C. H. Yeaman and Miss D. Bentley,
St. Georges Chambers, Kingsway, Stoke-on-Trent.

On November 21st, 1929, the North Staffs Branch listened to a Lecture on "Ultra Violet Ray Treatment and Appara- tus" by Mr. F. R. Bartlett, of Metro Vick Supplies, Ltd., London. Considerable interest was evinced in this lecture, and many questions were asked.
The last meeting in 1929 took the form of a Social Eve- ing, when a large number of members and their friends assembled at the Town Hall, Stoke-on-Trent, on December 12th. The proceedings opened with a concert, and after refreshments had been served, a whist drive and dance brought a bright and cheerful evening to a close.
The first Annual Meeting of the Branch was held on January 23rd, 1930. The President, Mrs. H. Leese, reviewed the work of the Branch during its first year, and was pleased to note the interest which was shown in the Association, evidenced both by the number of new members enrolled and the attendance at the meetings. At the close of the business meeting, Mr. A. Gould, Hon. Secretary of the Stoke Branch of the Electrical Contractors Association, gave a most in- structive lecture, entitled "Wiring in the Home."
The speaker at the monthly meeting in February was Mr. C. H. Yeaman, City Electrical Engineer, who spoke on "Tariffs, with special reference to Water Heating," a parti- cularly happy choice of subject at a time when a number of members, taking advantage of the low rates offered by the Multipart Tariff in the City, are installing electric water heating.
On February 27th, E.A.W. day at the British Industries Fair, a number of members journeyed to Castle Bromwich to visit the Heavy Section of the Fair. A most instructive and enjoyable day was spent there, and incidentally advantage was taken of the chance of meeting members of other Branches at tea.

***

Bristol and District Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Miss A. R. Wright, A.C.I.S.,
Electricity Offices, Colston Avenue, Bristol.

Since the last report, a series of interesting lectures has been given to the members of the Branch.
On December 10th, Mr. F. L. Thomas gave a lecture on "Protective Devices," and dealt with the need for fuses, the tracing of small faults, and the best steps to take in pre- venting and remedying them.
On January 7th, Miss G. Edbrooke, Cookery Demonstrator to the Bristol Corporation Electricity Department, gave a lecture-demonstration on Electric Cookery, which was well attended.
On January 20th, Mr. T. Catten gave a lantern lecture entitled "Electric Light and Eyesight Preservation," dealing mainly with the advantages of glareless light.
On February 6th, Mr. L. Burden gave a lecture on "The Application of Electricity in the Home," and illustrated his points by showing the inner workings of various pieces of domestic electrical apparatus.
In February also, Mr. L. E. Buckell gave his interesting lecture on "Colour Lighting for Home Decoration." As there was difficulty in obtaining a suitable room, the General Elec- tric Company very kindly placed their new Showroom at the service of the Branch, and by this means several experiments were made possible which would have been impracticable elsewhere. The G.E.C. very kindly provided coffee and a tempting assortment of electrically-cooked cakes.
On March 4th, Mr. A. M. Willis gave a lecture on "Electricity in the Service of Woman." After dealing with the past and present, Mr. Willis drew an ideal picture of the all-electric home as he saw it, and suggested that this might be the goal towards which the efforts of all members should be directed.
The Annual General Meeting was held on March 20th.
The arrangements for the summer fixtures are well in hand, and include a Garden Party and an Outing.
A.R.W.

TALK by Mr. Llewelyn B. Atkin- son, A.M.Inst.C.E., M.I.E.E. (Chairman of Royal Society of Arts), on "Some Electrical Reminiscences."

transcription:
The Electrical Age 653

Mid-Gloucestershire Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Miss G. Johnson, 21, Eastgate Street, Gloucester.

January 9th.—A most enjoyable and successful Thé Dansant was held at the Mercers Hall, Gloucester. Dancing commenced at 3 p.m., and continued until 8 p.m., with an interval for a dainty tea, which everyone enjoyed.
February 12th.—Mr. F. H. Corson, City Electrical En- gineer, Gloucester, gave us another interesting and instructive demonstration lecture on "The Treatment of Minor Troubles which may arise in Domestic Apparatus," showing what happens when an electric kettle boils dry, and how modern kettles disconnect themselves. Mr. Corson also showed the working of an electric iron and radiator, and dealt with the replacement of fuses, wiring of lampholders, etc. Delightful souvenir of leatherette cases containing 5 and 10 amp. fuse wires were given to the members.
February 25th.—Our First Annual Meeting and Luncheon was held at the Mercers Hall, Gloucester, when we were delighted to have the Director with us. The Annual General Meeting was presided over by the Chairman (Mrs. Ellis), in the unavoidable absence of our President (the Countess of Berkeley), who was in Rome. The Director briefly outlined the work of the Association.
The Luncheon proved a very delightful and pleasing function. We were fortunate in having among our guests the Mayor and Mayoress of Gloucester, Mr. W. T. Hobbs, Mr. F. H. Corson, Mr. and Mrs. W. J. Bache (Cheltenham), Mr. H. S. Ellis, Mr. P. Gale and Mrs. R. J. Morris, the Deputy Lady Chairman and Hon. Secretary of the Cardiff Branch, the Vice-President and Hon. Secretary of the Chel- tenham Branch, and the Chairmen of the Bristol Branch. Toasts were very heartily proposed and responded to. Following the Luncheon a most interesting Lantern Lecture was given by Mr. H. S. Ellis on "The Development of an Electrical Power Company."
G. JOHNSON.

***

North Staffordshire Branch.
Joint Hon. Secretaries:
Mrs. C. H. Yeaman and Miss D. Bentley,
St. Georges Chambers, Kingsway, Stoke-on-Trent.

On November 21st, 1929, the North Staffs Branch listened to a Lecture on "Ultra Violet Ray Treatment and Appara- tus" by Mr. F. R. Bartlett, of Metro Vick Supplies, Ltd., London. Considerable interest was evinced in this lecture, and many questions were asked.
The last meeting in 1929 took the form of a Social Eve- ing, when a large number of members and their friends assembled at the Town Hall, Stoke-on-Trent, on December 12th. The proceedings opened with a concert, and after refreshments had been served, a whist drive and dance brought a bright and cheerful evening to a close.
The first Annual Meeting of the Branch was held on January 23rd, 1930. The President, Mrs. H. Leese, reviewed the work of the Branch during its first year, and was pleased to note the interest which was shown in the Association, evidenced both by the number of new members enrolled and the attendance at the meetings. At the close of the business meeting, Mr. A. Gould, Hon. Secretary of the Stoke Branch of the Electrical Contractors Association, gave a most in- structive lecture, entitled "Wiring in the Home."
The speaker at the monthly meeting in February was Mr. C. H. Yeaman, City Electrical Engineer, who spoke on "Tariffs, with special reference to Water Heating," a parti- cularly happy choice of subject at a time when a number of members, taking advantage of the low rates offered by the Multipart Tariff in the City, are installing electric water heating.
On February 27th, E.A.W. day at the British Industries Fair, a number of members journeyed to Castle Bromwich to visit the Heavy Section of the Fair. A most instructive and enjoyable day was spent there, and incidentally advantage was taken of the chance of meeting members of other Branches at tea.

***

Bristol and District Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Miss A. R. Wright, A.C.I.S.,
Electricity Offices, Colston Avenue, Bristol.

Since the last report, a series of interesting lectures has been given to the members of the Branch.
On December 10th, Mr. F. L. Thomas gave a lecture on "Protective Devices," and dealt with the need for fuses, the tracing of small faults, and the best steps to take in pre- venting and remedying them.
On January 7th, Miss G. Edbrooke, Cookery Demonstrator to the Bristol Corporation Electricity Department, gave a lecture-demonstration on Electric Cookery, which was well attended.
On January 20th, Mr. T. Catten gave a lantern lecture entitled "Electric Light and Eyesight Preservation," dealing mainly with the advantages of glareless light.
On February 6th, Mr. L. Burden gave a lecture on "The Application of Electricity in the Home," and illustrated his points by showing the inner workings of various pieces of domestic electrical apparatus.
In February also, Mr. L. E. Buckell gave his interesting lecture on "Colour Lighting for Home Decoration." As there was difficulty in obtaining a suitable room, the General Elec- tric Company very kindly placed their new Showroom at the service of the Branch, and by this means several experiments were made possible which would have been impracticable elsewhere. The G.E.C. very kindly provided coffee and a tempting assortment of electrically-cooked cakes.
On March 4th, Mr. A. M. Willis gave a lecture on "Electricity in the Service of Woman." After dealing with the past and present, Mr. Willis drew an ideal picture of the all-electric home as he saw it, and suggested that this might be the goal towards which the efforts of all members should be directed.
The Annual General Meeting was held on March 20th.
The arrangements for the summer fixtures are well in hand, and include a Garden Party and an Outing.
A.R.W.

The E.A.W.

11.15 a.m.—Annual General Meeting of Mem- bers, Park Lane Hotel, Piccadilly, W.1.
1 p.m.—LUNCHEON, Park Lane Hotel.
3.30 p.m.—VISIT to the HOME OFFICE INDUSTRIAL MUSEUM, Horseferry Road, S.W.1.
8 p.m.—RECEPTION by the London Executive Committee, at the Institu- tion of Electrical Engineers, Savoy Place, Victoria Embankment, W.C.2.
TALK by Mr. Llewelyn B. Atkin- son, A.M.Inst.C.E., M.I.E.E. (Chairman of Royal Society of Arts), on "Some Electrical Reminiscences."

FRIDAY, MAY 16th, 1930.
10.30 a.m.—VISIT to Messrs. J. Lyons & Co.s Factory at Greenford.
9 p.m.—2 a.m.—BALL, Park Lane Hotel. Mrs. Wilfrid Ashley will receive the Guests.

Yeaman, City Electrical Engineer, who spoke on "Tariffs, with special reference to Water Heating," a parti- cularly happy choice of subject at a time when a number of members, taking advantage of the low rates offered by the Multipart Tariff in the City, are installing electric water heating.
On February 27th, E.A.W. day at the British Industries Fair, a number of members journeyed to Castle Bromwich to visit the Heavy Section of the Fair. A most instructive and enjoyable day was spent there, and incidentally advantage was taken of the chance of meeting members of other Branches at tea.

transcription:
652	The Electrical Age

East Devon Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Miss Wilson, 181, Sidwell Street, Exeter.
When the East Devon Branch was inaugurated, in October last, the district covered included Torquay, Newton Abbot and Teignmouth, and we feel very proud that within such a short time our Torquay friends have decided to launch out in a Branch of their own. Their Inaugural Meeting on February 8th is a very happy memory to the representatives of the East Devon Branch who attended, and we wish them every success during their forthcoming activities.
Our visit to the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital, by kind invitation of Dr. Miller Muir, was by far the most inter-esting since the formation of the Branch. It is very encour-aging to learn that electricity is doing so much to alleviate the sufferings of mankind, and we are particularly indebted to such as Dr. Miller Muir, who are giving their best efforts in the service of humanity.
Other meetings during the past three months include a visit to the Newton Abbot Power Station, by kind invitation of the Torquay Electricity Committee; a lecture and demonstration by Miss Wilson, entitled "Electric Housewifery"; also a repetition of the lecture held earlier in the session in Torquay, on "Electric Light and Eyesight Preser-vation," by Mr. F. Marsh, of the E.L.M.A. Lighting Service Bureau.

Joint Local Hon. Secretaries: Mrs. A. L. Goodall and
Miss M. Hellyer, Bedford Villa, Bedford Terrace, Plymouth.
Our Winter Session opened with a lecture by the City Electrical Engineer on "The Production and Utilization of Electrical Energy." This was given at the Showrooms of the General Electric Co., where members availed themselves of the excellent opportunity to inspect the many electrical ap-pliances on view. Refreshments kindly provided by the Company were greatly appreciated by our members.
The next event was a visit to the City Electricity Works, where members were able to see for themselves the plant used in the production of electrical energy. On this occasion tea was kindly provided by Mr. R. Lovell Dunstan, Chairman of the Electricity Committee.
Another interesting lecture was given by Mr. J. A. Goodall on "Whats a Watt?" We are looking forward to a visit to an electrically-equipped bakery.
Our membership is increasing steadily, and all lectures have been well attended.

***

London Activities.
The Spring fixtures have been very well attended, from the first visit in January to the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Hospital. Members were received by Dr. Eva White, one of the earliest Founder Members of the E.A.W. A vote of thanks was proposed by Miss Phyllis Atkinson during tea, kindly provided by Dr. White and the Matron.
The visit to the Richmond Home and Household Benefit Laundry, Ltd., by invitation of Mr. Chas. Brown, was a revelation to the many members present of what an up-to-date electric laundry is, and how it does its work. A vote of thanks to Mr. Brown, who also entertained the party to tea, was proposed by Mrs. J. F. Stanley.
Two Lectures, widely different in subject, but of equal interest, were given by Mr. R. Francis and Mr. L. L. Robinson, M.I.E.E.
Mr. R. S. Francis spoke on "Pl-able Lighting and Modern Architecture: Changing Styles in Cities and Homes," and the various periods were excellently demonstrated by fascin-ating lantern slides. This lecture was given at the E.L.M.A. Lighting Service Bureau, with Mr. Wilfrid Ashley in the chair, and the British Electrical Development Association kindly provided tea.
In an excellent and simple paper, Mr. Robinson explained the different tariffs and the many ways of arriving at assess-ments for the two-part tariff. He also gave particulars of tariffs used in other countries, but not tried here, and a good discussion followed, opened by Mrs. Hammer. A vote of thanks to the speaker was proposed by Miss Gladys Sharp.
The Socials have been so popular that the Social Sub-Committee have decided to arrange an Evening Social on April 9th, at the E.A.W. Club Room. During the evening Mr. J. F. Stanley, B.Sc., A.M.I.E.E., will give a short Lantern Talk on "A Holiday in Southern Spain and Morocco."
The members and friends who have attended the Socials will be interested to know that the Social Sub-Committee have sent a contribution of £5 to the Electrical Trades Benevolent Institution.
Two further visits this Session are to take place on March 27th and April 3rd. On the former day a large party will visit the Ediswan Works at Ponders End and the fol-lowing week is the visit to the Ideal Home Exhibition.
The General Electric Company, Ltd., have kindly invited us this year, and parties are coming from the Branches.
The programme for the day includes an inspection of the Pavilion of Light, and Luncheon at the Clarendon Hotel.
Members are also invited to the Ediswan "Hall of Ideals," and The Edison Swan Electric Co., Ltd., will enter-tain the party to tea.
V.N.

We are now looking forward to two country meetings, one a visit to the Cheriton Fitzpaine Electricity Undertaking, and an electrically-driven butter factory, and another in June, when we join with the Torquay and Plymouth Branches in a joint social event of some kind.

***

Hartlepools and District Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Mrs. J. H. Parker,
5, The Cliffs, Seaton Carew, co. Durham.
Our first visit this year was to the North Tees Power Station on January 11th. As this is one of the super-stations, many of our members results were so interested that the Company extended their invitation to them, and a party of about 30 went in special buses the eight miles to the station. We were conducted round in parties of 10 by members of the staff, who explained everything possible to us, and at the end thoroughly enjoyed the tea in which the Company entertained us.
On January 31st, Mr. S. Tillotson gave an instructive talk on "Bells, Batteries and Wireless Sets," to about 30 members in the Electricity Offices.
A visit in which all our members were extremely inter-ested was to Hartlepool Hospital on February 4th. Dr. Lithco and Mr. MacNab were most kind in demonstrating and ex-plaining the wonderful uses of electricity in medical and surgical work, after which we had tea with the Matron.
On February 27th we visited the South Durham Steel Works, and saw the entire process of steel-making: rough ice into white hot liquid which is poured into moulds to make huge red-hot blocks; these are rolled and rolled by electrically-operated rollers until they are thin sheets for shipbuilding.
The same evening, our Chairman, Councillor Mrs. Wilson, invited members to her house, and over 40 spent a very pleasant musical evening, in the course of which Lady Gray, President of the Branch, presented Mrs. J. H. Parker with a very beautiful cut glass electric table lamp, subscribed for by the members, as a farewell gift before Mrs. Parker left West Hartlepool for London.

***

Edinburgh and District Branch.
Hon. Secretary: Miss M. McNicol,
50, Frederick Street, Edinburgh.
The Edinburgh Branch commenced its activities in January, when an address on "The Elementary Principles of Electricity" was delivered by Mr. B. A. Pilkington.
Since then the Branch has been particularly successful, and a large number of members have been enrolled. In view of the increased membership, a visit was made to the Porto-bello Power Station, the members being personally conducted by Mr. E. Seddon, Engineer and Manager. Mr. W. Duncan, of the Corporation Electricity Department, explained how the housewife was considered by simplifying for her the charges for such technical items as volts, amperes and units into a single money standard. The Corporations ex-tremely moderate charges for lighting and power were favour-ably commented on by the members.
The demonstration of cooking by electricity was exceed-ingly popular, and was characterised by one of the members as the most modern and the most efficient method in use to-day.
On March 7th, a whist drive was held, and the large number of people who took part testified to the popularity of the young Branch. The prizes were presented by Mrs. A. Pratt. The presence of some members of the Glasgow Branch caused Miss McNicol to remark that the linking up of the East and the West electrically, which is to take place on April 30th, had been forestalled by the Women socially.
M. McNICOLL.

***

Plymouth and District Branch.
Joint Local Hon. Secretaries: Mrs. A. L. Goodall and
Miss M. Hellyer, Bedford Villa, Bedford Terrace, Plymouth.
Our Winter Session opened with a lecture by the City Electrical Engineer on "The Production and Utilization of Electrical Energy." This was given at the Showrooms of the General Electric Co., where members availed themselves of the excellent opportunity to inspect the many electrical ap-pliances on view. Refreshments kindly provided by the Company were greatly appreciated by our members.
The next event was a visit to the City Electricity Works, where members were able to see for themselves the plant used in the production of electrical energy. On this occasion tea was kindly provided by Mr. R. Lovell Dunstan, Chairman of the Electricity Committee.
Another interesting lecture was given by Mr. J. A. Goodall on "Whats a Watt?" We are looking forward to a visit to an electrically-equipped bakery.
Our membership is increasing steadily, and all lectures have been well attended.

***

London Activities.
The Spring fixtures have been very well attended, from the first visit in January to the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Hospital. Members were received by Dr. Eva White, one of the earliest Founder Members of the E.A.W. A vote of thanks was proposed by Miss Phyllis Atkinson during tea, kindly provided by Dr. White and the Matron.
The visit to the Richmond Home and Household Benefit Laundry, Ltd., by invitation of Mr. Chas. Brown, was a revelation to the many members present of what an up-to-date electric laundry is, and how it does its work. A vote of thanks to Mr. Brown, who also entertained the party to tea, was proposed by Mrs. J. F. Stanley.
Two Lectures, widely different in subject, but of equal interest, were given by Mr. R. Francis and Mr. L. L. Robinson, M.I.E.E.
Mr. R. S. Francis spoke on "Pl-able Lighting and Modern Architecture: Changing Styles in Cities and Homes," and the various periods were excellently demonstrated by fascin-ating lantern slides. This lecture was given at the E.L.M.A. Lighting Service Bureau, with Mr. Wilfrid Ashley in the chair, and the British Electrical Development Association kindly provided tea.
In an excellent and simple paper, Mr. Robinson explained the different tariffs and the many ways of arriving at assess-ments for the two-part tariff. He also gave particulars of tariffs used in other countries, but not tried here, and a good discussion followed, opened by Mrs. Hammer. A vote of thanks to the speaker was proposed by Miss Gladys Sharp.
The Socials have been so popular that the Social Sub-Committee have decided to arrange an Evening Social on April 9th, at the E.A.W. Club Room. During the evening Mr. J. F. Stanley, B.Sc., A.M.I.E.E., will give a short Lantern Talk on "A Holiday in Southern Spain and Morocco."
The members and friends who have attended the Socials will be interested to know that the Social Sub-Committee have sent a contribution of £5 to the Electrical Trades Benevolent Institution.
Two further visits this Session are to take place on March 27th and April 3rd. On the former day a large party will visit the Ediswan Works at Ponders End and the fol-lowing week is the visit to the Ideal Home Exhibition.
The General Electric Company, Ltd., have kindly invited us this year, and parties are coming from the Branches.
The programme for the day includes an inspection of the Pavilion of Light, and Luncheon at the Clarendon Hotel.
Members are also invited to the Ediswan "Hall of Ideals," and The Edison Swan Electric Co., Ltd., will enter-tain the party to tea.
V.N.
